Messages.Author: Hakuron
Messages.Body:
Can "Inscription" be played by a non-Banu Haqim to put this equipment with a copy of "Hunger of Marduk" on a non-Banu Haqim?
And can the latter use this copy?

I guess the answer is "yes" in both cases, because "put" and "use" usually circumvent clan requirements, but I would like to be sure.

Thanks in advance!

Inscription
Cardtype: Equipment
Discipline: Thaumaturgy
Equipment.
[tha] Put this equipment on a ready vampire and put a card that requires Blood Sorcery [tha] from your hand on it (face up, out of play; this acting vampire pays the cost of that card). The vampire with this equipment can burn this equipment to use the basic Blood Sorcery ability of that card.
[THA] As above, but the vampire can use the superior Blood Sorcery [THA] ability of the card.

Hunger of Marduk
Cardtype: Combat
Clan: Banu Haqim
Discipline: Thaumaturgy
Only usable before range is determined.
[tha] This round, this vampire can strike, ranged: steal 1 blood or life (becoming blood).
[THA] As above, but for 2 blood or life (becoming blood).

> For the card to work as ruled here it would need explicit text saying something like “play the card as if from your hand.” which it doesn’t.

I disagree about anything needing to be changed from the card.

Vampire with inscription is not playing the hunger of marduk. They are using an ability on the inscription (which copies the ability from the inscribed card). Since they are not playing the hunger of marduk, the play requirements do not matter.

Putting a card on inscription doesn't have any other requirements than blood sorcery (thaumaturgy), thus hunger of marduk can be put there.

Messages.Author: inm8
Messages.Body:
> Ankha wrote:
> No reversal for now, this ruling stands.
>
LSJ´s ruling is a contradiction to the fact that requirements are only relevant when "playing" a card and that they don´t apply when using a card.

This ruling insinuates that for example, only a Banu Haqim could make use of the effect provided by Path of Blood to take the action to burn it (i.e. the requirement of the card must be met to use its effect) which we all know is not the case.

I question the choice of keeping the ruling when it clearly is wrong, it would be better to at least issue a new ruling in its place.

Furthermore, seems to me counterintuitive that requirements are ignored when one gets to "put a card" on Inscription but has to meet them when using its effect... in other games, inscription is commonly used for the purpose of allowing a one-time use of an effect one normally doesn't master/meet the requirements for.

The Path of Blood

Cardtype: Master
Clan: Banu Haqim
Cost: 1 pool
Unique.
Put this card in play. Cards requiring Quietus [qui] cost Banu Haqim 1 fewer blood. Any minion can burn this card as a  action that inflicts 1 unpreventable environmental damage on acting vampires.

Messages.Author: Bloodartist
Messages.Body:
I do agree with inm8 in that LSJ ruling is contradictory to the card text.

The text says:
"The vampire with this equipment can burn this equipment to use the basic Blood Sorcery ability of that card."

It says "use" not "play". If requirements only apply when playing a card, then the requirements should not apply here. You are not playing the card from the inscription, you are using an ability on the card: inscription.

If the intent was different, inscription should say: "vampire with this equipment may play that card as if they had basic thaumaturgy blood sorcery".

> Requirements for Playing Cards
>
> Each library card has symbols on the attribute bar (the marble stripe on the left side) for the card type (except for master cards), the clan, or Discipline (if any) required to play the card, and the cost (if any) of playing that card.
>
> Some cards will have other requirements (such as capacity or title) stated in the card text. Only a minion who meets the requirements given on a minion card can play it, whereas only a Methuselah who controls a ready minion who meets the requirements of a master card can play it.
